items.entity: supports of the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that each sample has 1–4 supports drawn from 16 candidates: 4 corner nodes, 4 edge-midpoint nodes, and 8 node sets running from a corner to a midpoint. The text never says which ones the row-1 sample uses. Fig. 5 is unavailable, and its caption says it shows topologies only. Also, if only a single point support were drawn, the structure could rotate freely about that node; the text does not say how such draws were handled. Positions below are fractions of side L, origin bottom-left, y up.

items.entity: unit point load of the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1: the load sits on a randomly chosen element along the boundary of the 64×64 grid. The text does not say which edge or which element for row 1. At best it could be guessed from the ground-truth image in Fig. 5, which is not available.
readings: bottom edge (y=0), element i, at x/L≈(i+0.5)/64, i=0..63
right edge (x=L), element j, at y/L≈(j+0.5)/64, j=0..63
top edge (y=L), element i, at x/L≈(i+0.5)/64, i=0..63
left edge (x=0), element j, at y/L≈(j+0.5)/64, j=0..63

items.entity: direction of the point load in the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1: the direction is one of '6 evenly distributed angles' between 0 and 360°. The row-1 angle is not given. The data were also augmented by rotating and mirroring, so a sample rotated by 90° would have its angle at an odd multiple of 30°.
readings: odd multiple of 30° (30/90/150/210/270/330°) if the sample is a 90°-rotated copy
72°, 144°, 216° or 288° if the angle set is linspace(0,360,6)

items.entity: target volume fraction of the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1: the volume fraction is randomly sampled between 30% and 50%. The text does not say whether it is continuous or stepped, and the row-1 value is not given. It could only be estimated from the share of solid pixels in the unseen ground-truth image.

items.entity: definition of the 6-angle set and angle convention
items.description: Sec. 4.1, 'sampled from an angle of 0 to 360° from 6 evenly distributed angles', can mean 60° spacing that excludes 360°. It can also mean linspace with the endpoint included: 72° spacing where 0° and 360° coincide, giving only 5 distinct directions. The reference axis and the direction of rotation (math axes vs. image axes with y pointing down) are not stated.
readings: same sets measured clockwise (image coordinates, y down)

items.entity: how the unit load on a boundary element becomes nodal forces
items.description: Sec. 4.1 and Eq. 24 attach the load to an element (F_e). A finite-element solver needs nodal forces, and the text does not say whether the force goes to one node, the element's two outer-edge nodes, or all four of its nodes.
readings: full unit force on one node of the element (e.g., an outer-edge node)
split 0.5/0.5 between the element's two outer-edge nodes
split 0.25 to each of the element's 4 nodes

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'the sets of nodes between corners and midpoints'. With 65 nodes per edge, it does not say whether the corner node and the midpoint node at each end belong to the set.
No filter type or radius is given for the SIMP runs that produced the dataset. Sec. 4.1 mentions only a 'Heaviside filter'.

Sec. 4.1 says only 'with a Heaviside filter to ensure binary output images'. It could be a projection inside the optimization loop, in which case its sharpness (β), threshold (η), schedule for increasing β, and whether the volume limit applies to the projected densities are all missing. Or it could be a threshold applied to the converged densities afterwards.
readings: projection inside the loop, η = 0.5, β doubled from 1 to 32/64
post-processing threshold of converged densities at 0.5
post-processing threshold chosen to meet volume fraction f

items.description: Sec. 2.1 says only that p is 'commonly set to 3'. The value or ramp-up schedule used for the dataset is never stated.
Eq. 5 uses E_min but gives no value.
Sec. 2.1 says the sensitivities 'can be used in an optimization algorithm such as MMA'. The update scheme and move limit actually used for the dataset are not stated.
Eq. 7 gives the form of the relative-compliance-change test but no tolerance ε. Sec. 2.1 also mentions iteration-count limits without giving a value.
The starting design is not stated. Sec. 1 itself notes that SIMP results are sensitive to the initial guess.

items.entity: Young's modulus E0 in the SIMP optimization
items.description: E = 1 and ν = 0.3 are stated only for the pre-processing analysis that builds the input fields (Sec. 4.1). They are not explicitly tied to the topology-optimization runs, though ν = 0.3 is presumably the same.
readings: another E0 value with ν = 0.3 (compliance scales by 1/E0)

items.description: The text does not say whether plane stress or plane strain was used, the element thickness, or the element formulation (the 'square elements' are presumably standard 4-node bilinear elements).
readings: plane stress, unit thickness, 4-node bilinear elements
plane stress, non-unit thickness (compliance scales by 1/t)

items.entity: elements at the load or supports
items.description: No fixed-solid or fixed-void regions are mentioned. The load-discrepancy metric (Eq. 24) expects material at the load element, but the text does not say whether this was enforced in the SIMP runs.
readings: boundary element under the load fixed solid

items.entity: orientation and augmentation of the displayed row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says samples were augmented by rotation and mirroring. The text does not say whether row 1 is an original or a transformed sample, or how image rows map to the solver's y-axis. This matters when reading supports and load from the figure and for which load angles are possible.
readings: figure shown in solver axes (x right, y up)
figure in image axes (row 0 at top), i.e., flipped vertically relative to the solver
